Daisy chain the platinum delivery:Put one diver near the supply, one diver in the middle, one diver at the box and another roaming. As a launch day diver, there is a pretty fair argument that the game is easier now. The difference isn't that players suddenly got better — the games had some changesRemember when Chargers took multiple Recoilless Rifle headshots to kill? Bile Titans could take 4–5 rockets? That's why the Railgun leg meta existed. The alternatives simply weren't as reliable. The bot front was the same story: Automatons had extremely accurate long-range fire, ragdoll chains could keep you airborne or rolling helplessly across the ground, and the Spear was practically unusable for months because of its lock-on issues. We fought the Creek without the tools we have now.Before Patch 01.000.400 there were also significantly more heavy spawns, so missions demanded a very specific anti-heavy setup.Today we have far more options, and many threats can be deleted with the right tool. Team reloads make heavy weapons even stronger, and the overall arsenal is much more capable. The newer enemy variants like spore and rupture strains are actually a good direction because they add pressure without just being another bullet sponge. Remember spore is countered by fire. fire deaths are not suppose to trigger there speed boost. Oshaune was a great example — extremely difficult, but also one of the most memorable and fun campaigns, which is why it became the bloodiest battle.The funny thing is that most deaths now usually aren't from the big monsters anymore; they're from getting overwhelmed by chaff. The balance has almost flipped. Chargers, Bile Titans, Hulks, and Factory Striders, vox are rarely the thing that kills experienced players — it's getting pinned, surrounded, or caught out of position.And yes, you can absolutely clear D10 with only the base Warbond and level-unlocked Stratagems. The game gives you everything you need: Autocannon, EATs, Recoilless, Spear, Eagle Airstrike, Orbital Precision Strike, MG-43, etc. Warbonds add variety and convenience, but they aren't a requirement for endgame contentAt the end of the day who cares about d10. 8 and 9 are fun. you can breath. you can collected samples for others. you get POI. You tools refresh faster than the enemies do. just have fun :)

Your aim sticks to rocks and obstacles due to parallax aiming mechanics, third-person gun barrel collision, and environmental soft-locks.Why Your Aim Snaps and SticksParallax and Barrel Pointing: The center dot on your screen shows where you look, but the small circle shows where your gun barrel actually points. When a rock is near your line of sight, the game forces your barrel aim to respect your character's physical position (which is often lower than the camera view), causing a soft-lock onto the obstacle.Third-Person Collision Geometry: Environmental assets have collision boundaries that interact with your weapon's raycast. If an object intersects the path between your Helldiver's gun tip and your target, the reticle snaps to the nearest geometry.In-Game Soft-Lock Bugs: Many players on community spaces like the Steam Community Discussions report that the third-person reticle erratically pulls toward edges and rocks even when a clear line of sight appears to exist.How to Bypass or Fix ItSwitch to First-Person (ADS): Clicking your aim-down-sights (ADS) button forces the camera to look straight down the actual barrel, bypassing third-person parallax and freeing your reticle from environmental snapping.Crouch or Go Prone: Lowering your stance changes your physical gun alignment relative to low cover, reducing the awkward vertical pull caused by standing right behind a rock.Reposition Your Diver: Take a step back or move sideways away from the edge of the rock to clear your character model's physical line of fire from the collision mesh.It just took me 2 minutes of research... instead of arguing for hours...
